cells.title: Honour the escalate flag when the plan assigns a role
cells.action: Per D1 (issues 109, 111, 113). In verbs/drivers/prepare.rs the line `let escalated_cell = role.is_none()` (inside the role resolution block, just after the comment that starts `D5 (store 97ce5225)`) tests the `role` variable, but `let role = if role.is_some() { role } else { v2_effective_role.as_deref() };` earlier fills `role` with the approved plan's planned role, so on any v2-plan feature an escalated cell never escalates and gets the herding command. Make the check use the caller's own flag (`orig_role`, set by `let orig_role = role;`) instead of the role that the v2 plan filled, so an explicit --role still outranks the flag but a planned role does not. Make sure the v2 path does not then refuse the escalated dispatch as planned_role_mismatch and that the payload carries no herding command and no model param (Resolved::Inherit). Red first: in verbs/drivers/tests.rs add a test that builds a v2-plan feature (copy the fixture shape of an existing v2 planned_role test — rg -n planned_role verbs/drivers/tests.rs) whose cell role resolves to a herding slot, sets the cell `escalate: true`, runs prepare --kind cell, and asserts the payload is not a Bash herding command; watch it fail before the fix. Keep every existing prepare test green. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: an escalated cell on a feature with a v2 role plan gets a session-model payload with no herding command
an explicit --role still outranks the escalate flag

cells.title: Break a stale claim gate so unclaim and reopen free the claim
cells.action: Per D2 (issue 108). `unclaim_cell`, `run_reopen` and `run_drop` in verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs already pass clear_claim_after=true to `mutate_cell`, which calls `release_claim_file_best_effort(root, id)` (verbs/cells/claims.rs). That helper returns silently when `acquire_gate` returns false (`return Ok(()); // GATE_HELD — best-effort caller never retries`). The gate is the create-new file `.bee/claims/<id>.adopting` holding `{"pid":…,"at":…}`; when a claiming process dies between acquire_gate and release_gate the file stays for ever (this repo has stale det-1/det-2/det-3/rel530-1/rel540-1/rel550-1 .adopting files, det-2's dated at the exact #108 claim time), so every later release skips and the claim row outlives the unclaim. Fix in claims.rs: when `acquire_gate` meets an existing gate file, treat it as stale and remove it (then try once more) when its `at` is older than 30 seconds, or its pid is not alive (on unix check /proc/<pid> or libc-free `std::path::Path::new("/proc").join(pid)` existence; on other targets use age only), or the file does not parse. Make `release_claim_file_best_effort` use `acquire_gate_with_retry` so a briefly-held live gate is waited out. Never break a fresh gate held by a live pid. Red first in verbs/cells/tests.rs: claim a cell (use the existing claim fixture — rg -n "fn .*claim" verbs/cells/tests.rs), write a stale `<id>.adopting` (pid 999999999, at one hour ago), run unclaim, and assert the claim file under .bee/claims is gone and a second claim succeeds; watch it fail before the fix. Add a test that a fresh gate with the current pid is not broken. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: after cells unclaim the claim store row is gone even when a stale .adopting gate was left by a dead claimer
a second cells claim on the unclaimed cell succeeds
a fresh gate held by a live process is never broken

artifacts.substantive: stale-gate unclaim test that failed before the fix

key_links: acquire_gate breaks a stale gate; release_claim_file_best_effort retries
prohibitions: No change to the ownership guard

cells.title: Keep the permit session for deploy workers, name the right Paseo FIX, gate the unix test helper
cells.action: Three fixes in herding/run.rs. (1) Per D3 (issues 103, 112): `pub(crate) fn build_child_env(` strips every SESSION_ENV_VARS entry after merging the passthrough (the loop after the line `// Strip leader session IDs even if present in passthrough or agent_env`), so a Paseo deploy worker never gets the issuer `BEE_SESSION_ID` and `bee dispatch authorize` refuses deploy_authorization_wrong_session. Keep the strip, then re-insert `BEE_SESSION_ID` from `passthrough` only when `passthrough` also holds a non-empty `BEE_DISPATCH_ID` (the herdr pane path already exports it — see PASSTHROUGH_ENV_VARS). CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and PI_SESSION_ID stay stripped always. In herding/tests.rs keep `child_env_construction_excludes_leader_session_and_sets_worker_marker` passing and add a test: passthrough with BEE_DISPATCH_ID and BEE_SESSION_ID gives the child BEE_SESSION_ID and no PI_SESSION_ID; passthrough with BEE_SESSION_ID but no BEE_DISPATCH_ID gives none. (2) Per D4 (issue 98): in `execute_paseo`, the `Err(e)` arm of `cli.call_as_caller(&argv)` always appends `— FIX: start the daemon with paseo daemon start (npm @getpaseo/cli 0.10.3+)`. Append that FIX only when the daemon does not answer. The same arm already makes a follow-up `cli.call(&paseo::ls_label_argv(&label))`; when that call returns Ok the daemon answered, so append instead a FIX that tells the user to check the agent's provider and model in the herding agent config (name the agent); when it returns Err keep the daemon-start FIX. Do not use paseo::daemon_reachable() (a real TCP probe). Tests use the existing fake PaseoCli, which controls the ls reply: follow the existing test that asserts the daemon FIX (rg -n "FIX: start the daemon" herding/run.rs) and add one where ls answers Ok. (2b) A deploy worker now carries the leader's BEE_SESSION_ID; `run_session_release` in verbs/state_group/sessions.rs must not release the leader from inside a herding worker: when BEE_HERDING_WORKER is "1" and no --session-id flag is given, return a typed no-op (released:false, reason herding_worker) without writing. Test it with crate::hooks::herding_env_lock() held. (3) Per D5 (issue 96): `fn seed_claude_guard(` in the test module uses `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt` and breaks the Windows build; mark it and every test that calls it `#[cfg(unix)]`. Red first for (1) and (2). No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: a child env built with BEE_DISPATCH_ID and BEE_SESSION_ID in the passthrough carries BEE_SESSION_ID
without BEE_DISPATCH_ID no leader session variable reaches the child
a paseo run error from a live daemon does not name the daemon-start FIX
seed_claude_guard and its callers compile only on unix
bee state session release run inside a herding worker without --session-id releases nothing

prohibitions: No real paseo call in tests

cells.action: Per D11 (issue 100). `pub fn compute_verify_skill_items(` in onboard/plan.rs pushes `copy_verify_skill` for any installed projection where `verify_skill_drifted(&source_walk, &target_walk)` is true, so `onboard --apply` replaces host edits. cells.title: Keep the concurrent-worker git guard on inside a herded worker
cells.action: Per D13 (issue 116). In hooks/mod.rs `try_native` returns success for every hook but `activity` and `worker-guard` when BEE_HERDING_WORKER is set (`if herding_worker_marker_set() && marker_short_circuits(&name) {`, herding-worker-standalone D3: a herded worker gets no guards). The Pi bee-guard extension calls only `bee hook write-guard`, so a herded Pi worker runs `git stash`, `git reset`, `git checkout` and the other whole-tree verbs with no check, even while sibling workers hold uncommitted work in the same worktree (seen: a worker's `git stash push` swept three siblings' edits). Keep D3 for everything else, but under the marker let `write-guard` run ONE narrow check: for a Bash tool call, tokenize the command (tokenize_deep), find each git invocation (paths.rs `find_git_invocations`), classify it with `classify_concurrent_tree_verb` (paths.rs), and when a whole-tree verb is found resolve the live worker count with `resolve_live_worker_count` (paths.rs) for the worktree the payload cwd names; deny with the same `concurrent_tree_refusal` text and remedy the full guard uses when the count is above one (and when it cannot be resolved), else allow. Every other tool and every other check stays a silent success under the marker. Put the new function in a new file hooks/write_guard/worker_tree.rs declared in hooks/write_guard/mod.rs; do not edit checks.rs or paths.rs (read-only reuse; make a helper pub(crate) only if it is not yet reachable, and record that as a deviation). Use the existing fixtures that build live-worker reservations for the full guard's concurrent-tree tests (rg -n concurrent hooks/write_guard/tests.rs). No code comments. cells.title: Break a stale claim gate so unclaim and reopen free the claim
cells.action: Per D2 (issue 108). `unclaim_cell`, `run_reopen` and `run_drop` in verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs already pass clear_claim_after=true to `mutate_cell`, which calls `release_claim_file_best_effort(root, id)` (verbs/cells/claims.rs). That helper returns silently when `acquire_gate` returns false (`return Ok(()); // GATE_HELD — best-effort caller never retries`). The gate is the create-new file `.bee/claims/<id>.adopting` holding `{"pid":…,"at":…}`; when a claiming process dies between acquire_gate and release_gate the file stays for ever (this repo has stale det-1/det-2/det-3/rel530-1/rel540-1/rel550-1 .adopting files, det-2's dated at the exact #108 claim time), so every later release skips and the claim row outlives the unclaim. Fix in claims.rs: when `acquire_gate` meets an existing gate file, treat it as stale and remove it (then try once more) when its `at` is older than 30 seconds, or its pid is not alive (on unix check /proc/<pid> or libc-free `std::path::Path::new("/proc").join(pid)` existence; on other targets use age only), or the file does not parse. Make `release_claim_file_best_effort` use `acquire_gate_with_retry` so a briefly-held live gate is waited out. Never break a fresh gate held by a live pid. Red first in verbs/cells/tests.rs: claim a cell (use the existing claim fixture — rg -n "fn .*claim" verbs/cells/tests.rs), write a stale `<id>.adopting` (pid 999999999, at one hour ago), run unclaim, and assert the claim file under .bee/claims is gone and a second claim succeeds; watch it fail before the fix. Add a test that a fresh gate with the current pid is not broken. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

cells.title: Keep the concurrent-worker git guard on inside a herded worker
cells.action: Per D13 (issue 116). In hooks/mod.rs `try_native` returns success for every hook but `activity` and `worker-guard` when BEE_HERDING_WORKER is set (`if herding_worker_marker_set() && marker_short_circuits(&name) {`, herding-worker-standalone D3: a herded worker gets no guards). Every other tool and every other check stays a silent success under the marker.
